Two flyovers, one shared clock

Aircraft Doppler matching with a shared recording clock. Inspect the signal, compare alternatives, and decide what the evidence supports.

HYPOTHESIS ONLY

A ranked hypothesis needs corroboration.

Accepted location: no. A high score means that predicted frequency curves follow bright structure in this spectrogram. It does not establish that the aircraft or location is correct.

  • Scores are line contrast, not probabilities or calibrated confidence.
  • This is a bounded hypothesis search, not a verified location.
  • Source tone is assumed constant within each event; wind is not modeled.

01 / Read the signal

Time is relative to the first audio sample. Each event has its own source tone; all events share one clock offset. Persistent tones are reduced by temporal median subtraction.

02 / Compare locations

This is a score surface, not an uncertainty region. Unsupported grid points are gray. Grid spacing, track error, terrain, clock error and the acoustic model limit interpretation.

Greedy spatial alternatives separated by at least 300 m. The full grid is in candidates.csv; these alternatives are descriptive and are not independent statistical trials.

04 / Test the explanation

  1. Inspect each event separately.
  2. Repeat the complete search on reversed-time and noise controls.
  3. Change sound speed, clock bounds, event window and source frequency bounds.
  4. Validate against a held-out flyover or independently established recorder position.

Do not turn the score gap into a percentage confidence. Report unresolved alternatives.
